declarations.doc: Reassociating a right-associated triple alphabet back to the left preserves entropy.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_map_prodAssoc_symm

declarations.doc: Swapping the two coordinates of a joint law preserves joint entropy.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.jointEntropy_map_swap

declarations.doc: Joint entropy of two finite-valued random variables under a discrete law.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.jointEntropyOf

declarations.doc: Joint entropy of two random variables is invariant under swapping their order.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.jointEntropyOf_swap

declarations.doc: Entropy of three finite-valued random variables is invariant under reassociating the product alphabet.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropyOf_prodAssoc

declarations.doc: Finite Shannon entropy is bounded above by the logarithm of the alphabet size. The proof is Jensen's inequality for the concave function `Real.negMulLog`, applied with uniform weights over the finite alphabet.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_le_log_card

declarations.doc: Finite Shannon entropy is bounded by the logarithm of the number of atoms with nonzero mass. Unlike `entropy_le_log_card`, this theorem counts only the PMF support and does not require a separate nonempty-alphabet instance.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_le_log_support_ncard

declarations.doc: The entropy of a finite-valued random variable is bounded by the logarithm of the support size of its pushforward law.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropyOf_le_log_support_ncard

declarations.doc: The uniform distribution reaches the finite entropy upper bound. Mathematically, this is the equality case `H(U_alpha) = log |alpha|` for the uniform law on a nonempty finite alphabet.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_uniformOfFintype

declarations.doc: Finite Shannon entropy reaches the alphabet-cardinality bound exactly at the uniform distribution.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_eq_log_card_iff_eq_uniformOfFintype

declarations.doc: Finite Shannon entropy reaches its support-cardinality bound exactly when the distribution is uniform on its support.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_eq_log_support_ncard_iff_eq_uniformOnSupport

declarations.doc: A finite-valued random variable reaches the alphabet-cardinality entropy bound exactly when its law is uniform on the alphabet.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropyOf_eq_log_card_iff_map_eq_uniformOfFintype

declarations.doc: A finite-valued random variable reaches its law-support entropy bound exactly when that law is uniform on its support.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropyOf_eq_log_support_ncard_iff_map_eq_uniformOnSupport

declarations.doc: Entropy is concave under a finite PMF-valued selector. This is the general finite-selector form of the textbook binary entropy concavity inequality.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sum_mul_entropy_le_entropy_bind

declarations.doc: Entropy is concave under a binary PMF mixture.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.binaryMixture_entropy_concave

declarations.doc: For an interior binary weight, equality in entropy concavity holds exactly when the two component PMFs are equal.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.binaryMixture_entropy_eq_iff

declarations.doc: The Boolean error indicator for a deterministic decoder. It is `true` exactly when decoding the observation `y` does not recover the source symbol `x`. Decidable equality is chosen internally.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.decodingErrorIndicator

declarations.doc: The decoding-error indicator is `true` exactly on decoder failure.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.decodingErrorIndicator_eq_true_iff

declarations.doc: The decoding-error indicator is `false` exactly on decoder success.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.decodingErrorIndicator_eq_false_iff

declarations.doc: The probability that a deterministic decoder fails under a joint law. The PMF is a joint law of a source symbol and an observation, in that order.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.decodingErrorProbability

declarations.doc: The probability that a deterministic decoder fails for random variables. Here `X` is the source variable, `Y` is the observation, and `decoder` tries to recover `X` from `Y`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.decodingErrorProbabilityOf

declarations.doc: The decoding-error probability is the total mass of the joint atoms on which the decoder fails. This is the main finite-sum elimination theorem for decoding error.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.decodingErrorProbability_eq_sum

declarations.doc: A decoding-error probability is nonnegative.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.decodingErrorProbability_nonneg

declarations.doc: A decoding-error probability is at most one.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.decodingErrorProbability_le_one

declarations.doc: The decoding-error probability of random variables is nonnegative.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.decodingErrorProbabilityOf_nonneg

declarations.doc: The decoding-error probability of random variables is at most one.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.decodingErrorProbabilityOf_le_one

declarations.doc: The entropy, in nats, of the Boolean decoding-error indicator is the binary entropy of the decoding-error probability. The indicator is `true` exactly on decoder failure.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_decodingErrorIndicator

declarations.doc: The entropy, in nats, of a random variable's Boolean decoding-error indicator is the binary entropy of its decoding-error probability. Here `X` is the source variable, `Y` is the observation, and `decoder` attempts to recover `X` from `Y`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropyOf_decodingErrorIndicator

declarations.doc: Fano's inequality for a finite joint law and a deterministic decoder, in nats. Here the first coordinate is the source, the second coordinate is the observation, and `decoder` attempts to recover the source from the observation. The decoding-error indicator is `true` exactly when decoding fails. No lower bound on the source-alphabet cardinality is required; in particular, the singleton case is included.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_fano

declarations.doc: Fano's inequality for a finite joint law, expressed with mathlib's `Real.qaryEntropy`, in nats. The error convention and decoder direction are the same as in `condEntropy_fano`. This form is valid without a lower bound on the source alphabet cardinality.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_fano_qary

declarations.doc: The random-variable form of `condEntropy_fano`, in nats. Here `X` is the finite source variable, `Y` is the finite observation, and `decoder` attempts to recover `X` from `Y`. The error indicator is `true` exactly when decoding fails. The source sample space itself need not be finite.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf_fano

declarations.doc: The random-variable form of `condEntropy_fano_qary`, in nats. The decoder direction and error convention are those of `condEntropyOf_fano`. Only the value alphabets of `X` and `Y` must be finite.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf_fano_qary

declarations.doc: The conventional weaker form of Fano's inequality for a finite joint law: `H(X | Y) <= log 2 + Pe * log |alpha|`. All logarithms are natural, so `log 2` is the one-bit textbook constant expressed in nats. No lower bound on the source-alphabet cardinality is required.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_fano_weak

declarations.doc: The random-variable form of `condEntropy_fano_weak`, in nats. Only the finite value alphabets of `X` and `Y` are required; the source sample space may be arbitrary.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf_fano_weak

declarations.doc: Fano's lower bound on the decoding-error probability for a finite joint law: `(H(X | Y) - log 2) / log |alpha| <= Pe`. The hypothesis `2 <= |alpha|` is needed here, unlike in the entropy forms of Fano's inequality, because it makes the logarithmic denominator strictly positive.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.decodingErrorProbability_fano_lower_bound

declarations.doc: The random-variable form of `decodingErrorProbability_fano_lower_bound`. Only the finite value alphabets of `X` and `Y` are required. The source sample space may be arbitrary.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.decodingErrorProbabilityOf_fano_lower_bound

declarations.doc: Fano's mutual-information lower bound for a uniform finite source, in nats: `log |alpha| - log 2 - Pe * log |alpha| <= I(X;Y)`. The first marginal of the supplied joint law is the source law. No cardinality lower bound is needed because this theorem does not divide by `log |alpha|`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_fano_lower_bound_of_uniform_source

declarations.doc: The random-variable form of `mutualInfo_fano_lower_bound_of_uniform_source`. Uniformity is stated through the existing pushforward-law equality `p.map X = PMF.uniformOfFintype alpha`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf_fano_lower_bound_of_uniform_source

declarations.doc: The standard uniform-source Fano lower bound on decoding error, in nats: `1 - (I(X;Y) + log 2) / log |alpha| <= Pe`. The hypothesis `2 <= |alpha|` makes the logarithmic denominator strictly positive. Uniformity is expressed by equality of the first marginal with the existing finite uniform PMF.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.decodingErrorProbability_fano_lower_bound_of_uniform_source

declarations.doc: The random-variable form of `decodingErrorProbability_fano_lower_bound_of_uniform_source`. The sample space may be arbitrary; only the source and observation value alphabets are finite.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.decodingErrorProbabilityOf_fano_lower_bound_of_uniform_source

declarations.doc: The outcome type of the variables selected by the finite atom `s`. No finiteness assumption is needed to form this type. Pointwise finiteness of the selected alphabets is required only when taking entropy.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.FamilyOutcome

declarations.doc: The joint law of an indexed family of random variables under a source PMF. The source type, variable-name type, and full dependent outcome type may all be infinite.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyLawOf

declarations.doc: The joint marginal law of the variables selected by the finite atom `s`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMarginal

declarations.doc: Shannon entropy, in nats, of the variables selected by the finite atom `s`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropy

declarations.doc: Shannon entropy, in nats, of a finite subfamily of random variables under a source PMF.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropyOf

declarations.doc: Conditional entropy `H(A | B)` of two finite subfamilies. The atoms may overlap.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondEntropy

declarations.doc: Mutual information `I(A; B)` of two finite subfamilies. The atoms may overlap.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfo

declarations.doc: Conditional mutual information `I(A; B | C)` of three finite subfamilies. The three-way union is normalized as `(A ∪ B) ∪ C`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondMutualInfo

declarations.doc: Conditional entropy of two finite subfamilies under a source PMF.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondEntropyOf

declarations.doc: Mutual information of two finite subfamilies under a source PMF.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfoOf

declarations.doc: Conditional mutual information of three finite subfamilies under a source PMF.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondMutualInfoOf

declarations.doc: Restricting a finite family marginal to a smaller atom gives the marginal on that smaller atom.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMarginal_restrict

declarations.doc: The finite marginal of a source-indexed family is the joint law of its selected coordinates.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMarginal_familyLawOf

declarations.doc: Family entropy is ordinary random-variable entropy of finite restriction.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropy_eq_entropyOf

declarations.doc: Source-family entropy is ordinary entropy of the selected coordinates under the source law.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropyOf_eq_entropyOf

declarations.doc: Family entropy on `s` depends only on the source variables selected by `s`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropyOf_congr

declarations.doc: The entropy of the empty family is zero.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropy_empty

declarations.doc: The entropy of the empty source-indexed family is zero.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropyOf_empty

declarations.doc: The entropy of a singleton family is the entropy of that coordinate.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropy_singleton

declarations.doc: The entropy of a singleton source-indexed family is the entropy of that source variable.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropyOf_singleton

declarations.doc: Entropy of every finite subfamily is nonnegative.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropy_nonneg

declarations.doc: Entropy of every finite source-indexed subfamily is nonnegative.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropyOf_nonneg

declarations.doc: Entropy on a union is the joint entropy of the two restricted subfamilies. The atoms may overlap; no disjointness or support assumption is required.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropy_union

declarations.doc: Source-family entropy on a union is the joint entropy of the two selected subfamilies.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropyOf_union

declarations.doc: Entropy on a three-way union is entropy of the right-associated triple of restricted subfamilies. All three atoms may overlap.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropy_tripleUnion

declarations.doc: Source-family entropy on a three-way union is entropy of the right-associated triple of selected subfamilies.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropyOf_tripleUnion

declarations.doc: Family conditional entropy is ordinary conditional entropy of the two restriction-valued random variables.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondEntropy_eq_condEntropyOf

declarations.doc: Source-family conditional entropy is ordinary conditional entropy of the two selected subfamilies.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondEntropyOf_eq_condEntropyOf

declarations.doc: Family mutual information is ordinary mutual information of the two restriction-valued random variables.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfo_eq_mutualInfoOf

declarations.doc: Source-family mutual information is ordinary mutual information of the two selected subfamilies.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfoOf_eq_mutualInfoOf

declarations.doc: Family conditional mutual information is ordinary conditional mutual information of the three restriction-valued random variables.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondMutualInfo_eq_condMutualInfoOf

declarations.doc: Source-family conditional mutual information is ordinary conditional mutual information of the three selected subfamilies.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondMutualInfoOf_eq_condMutualInfoOf

declarations.doc: Singleton atoms recover conditional entropy of ordinary coordinates.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondEntropy_singletons

declarations.doc: Singleton source-family atoms recover conditional entropy of the corresponding ordinary random variables.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondEntropyOf_singletons

declarations.doc: Singleton atoms recover mutual information of ordinary coordinates.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfo_singletons

declarations.doc: Singleton source-family atoms recover mutual information of the corresponding ordinary random variables.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfoOf_singletons

declarations.doc: Singleton atoms recover conditional mutual information of ordinary coordinates.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondMutualInfo_singletons

declarations.doc: Singleton source-family atoms recover conditional mutual information of the corresponding ordinary random variables.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondMutualInfoOf_singletons

declarations.doc: Family mutual information is symmetric: `I(B;A) = I(A;B)`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfo_swap

declarations.doc: Source-family mutual information is symmetric.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfoOf_swap

declarations.doc: Family conditional mutual information is symmetric in its first two atoms: `I(B;A|C) = I(A;B|C)`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondMutualInfo_swap

declarations.doc: Source-family conditional mutual information is symmetric in its first two atoms.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondMutualInfoOf_swap

declarations.doc: Conditioning on the empty atom leaves family entropy unchanged.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondEntropy_empty_right

declarations.doc: The empty atom has zero conditional entropy.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondEntropy_empty_left

declarations.doc: Mutual information with the empty right atom is zero.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfo_empty_right

declarations.doc: Conditional mutual information with the empty second atom is zero.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondMutualInfo_empty_right

declarations.doc: Empty conditioning reduces conditional mutual information to mutual information.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondMutualInfo_empty_conditioning

declarations.doc: The mutual information of an atom with itself is its entropy.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfo_self

declarations.doc: Family mutual information as `I(A;B) = H(A) - H(A|B)`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfo_eq_entropy_sub_condEntropy

declarations.doc: Source-family mutual information as `I(A;B) = H(A) - H(A|B)`.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondMutualInfoOf_eq_condEntropyOf_sub_condEntropyOf

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropyOf_union_chain_rule_right

declarations.doc: Left-oriented source-family entropy chain rule.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropyOf_union_chain_rule_left

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfoOf_union_chain_rule

declarations.doc: Source-family conditional-mutual-information union chain rule.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondMutualInfoOf_union_chain_rule

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfoOf_eq_mutualInfoChain

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfo_chain_rule_of_nodup

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfoOf_chain_rule_of_nodup

declarations.doc: The zero-safe extended-real scalar term in the finite log-sum inequality. The conventions are `0 * log (0 / b) = 0` for every `b`, including `b = 0`, and `a * log (a / 0) = top` when `a` is positive.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.logSumTerm

declarations.doc: A zero numerator contributes zero to the extended log-sum.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.logSumTerm_zero_left

declarations.doc: A positive numerator over a zero denominator contributes `top`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.logSumTerm_pos_zero

declarations.doc: An extended log-sum term is never `bottom`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.logSumTerm_ne_bot

declarations.doc: Every finite selected sum of extended log-sum terms is never `bottom`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sum_logSumTerm_ne_bot

declarations.doc: Finite log-sum inequality with the zero-safe conventions of `logSumTerm`. In particular, a selected positive numerator over a zero denominator makes the right-hand side `top`; no support or positivity guard is required.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.logSum_inequality

declarations.doc: Equality in the zero-safe finite log-sum inequality. Equality holds exactly when all active selected pairs have one common `ENNReal` numerator-to-denominator ratio. Selected `(0, 0)` pairs are inactive; the common ratio may be finite or `top`.

declarations.doc: Equality in the guarded Real finite log-sum inequality holds exactly when all active selected pairs have one common finite ratio.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.real_logSum_eq_iff_exists_constant_ratio_of_support

declarations.doc: Conditional law of the first coordinate given a nonzero second-coordinate atom. Mathematically, this is the finite PMF `P_{A | B=b}(a) = P_{A,B}(a,b) / P_B(b)`. The proof argument `hb : sndMarginal p b ≠ 0` is part of the API so that zero-probability conditioning atoms do not receive a fake default distribution.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condFstGivenSnd

declarations.doc: Atom formula for the conditional law: `P_{A | B=b}(a) = P_{A,B}(a,b) / P_B(b)`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condFstGivenSnd_apply

declarations.doc: The conditional PMF does not depend on which proof of nonzero marginal mass was used to construct it.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condFstGivenSnd_proof_irrel

declarations.doc: An atom has zero conditional mass exactly when the corresponding joint atom has zero mass.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condFstGivenSnd_apply_eq_zero_iff

declarations.doc: An atom has nonzero conditional mass exactly when the corresponding joint atom has nonzero mass.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condFstGivenSnd_apply_ne_zero_iff

declarations.doc: The support of `P_{A | B=b}` is the fiber of the joint support over `b`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.support_condFstGivenSnd

declarations.doc: Joint mass factors as conditional mass times the conditioning marginal: `P_{A | B=b}(a) * P_B(b) = P_{A,B}(a,b)`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condFstGivenSnd_mul_sndMarginal

declarations.doc: Joint mass factors as the conditioning marginal times conditional mass: `P_B(b) * P_{A | B=b}(a) = P_{A,B}(a,b)`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal_mul_condFstGivenSnd

declarations.doc: Real-valued version of the joint factorization: `P_B(b) * P_{A | B=b}(a) = P_{A,B}(a,b)` after converting masses to `Real`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal_toReal_mul_condFstGivenSnd_toReal

declarations.doc: Entropy of the conditional fiber, with explicit zero-mass branch. This helper is intended for expected conditional entropy formulas. If `P_B(b)=0`, the branch is the number `0`, not the entropy of an arbitrary default conditional PMF.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyFstGivenSnd

declarations.doc: Zero-marginal conditioning atoms contribute zero to conditional-fiber entropy.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyFstGivenSnd_of_sndMarginal_eq_zero

declarations.doc: On nonzero conditioning atoms, `condEntropyFstGivenSnd` is the entropy of the canonical conditional PMF `P_{A | B=b}`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyFstGivenSnd_of_sndMarginal_ne_zero

declarations.doc: Per-fiber conditional entropy identity. For each conditioning atom `b`, `p_B(b) * H(P_{A | B=b}) = sum_a h(p(a,b)) - h(p_B(b))`, where `h(x) = -x log x`. If `p_B(b)=0`, the left side uses the explicit zero branch of `condEntropyFstGivenSnd`, and the right side is zero because every joint atom over `b` has zero mass.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal_toReal_mul_condEntropyFstGivenSnd

declarations.doc: Expected conditional entropy formula for the finite conditional-law API: `H(A | B) = sum_b p_B(b) * H(P_{A | B=b})`. The right-hand side is written using `condEntropyFstGivenSnd`, whose value is `0` on zero-marginal conditioning atoms and the entropy of the canonical conditional PMF on nonzero atoms.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_eq_sum_sndMarginal_mul_condEntropyFstGivenSnd

declarations.doc: The right-associated law `P_{A,B,C}` viewed as a law on `((A, B), C)`. This is the law whose conditional fibers over `C=c` are joint laws on `A × B`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.pairThirdLaw

declarations.doc: Atom formula for the reassociated law `((A,B),C)`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.pairThirdLaw_apply

declarations.doc: The second marginal of the reassociated law `((A,B),C)` is the law of `C`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal_pairThirdLaw

declarations.doc: Reassociating `(A,B,C)` as `((A,B),C)` preserves entropy.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_pairThirdLaw

declarations.doc: PMF form of the triple conditional-entropy chain rule: `H(A,B|C) = H(B|C) + H(A|B,C)`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_pairThirdLaw_chain_rule

declarations.doc: Swapped PMF form of the triple conditional-entropy chain rule: `H(A,B|C) = H(A|C) + H(B|A,C)`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_pairThirdLaw_chain_rule_swap

declarations.doc: Conditional joint law of the first two coordinates given a nonzero third coordinate atom. Mathematically, this is `P_{A,B | C=c}(a,b) = P_{A,B,C}(a,b,c) / P_C(c)`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condFstSndGivenThird

declarations.doc: Atom formula for `P_{A,B | C=c}`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condFstSndGivenThird_apply

declarations.doc: Joint mass factors through the conditional joint law: `P_C(c) * P_{A,B|C=c}(a,b) = P_{A,B,C}(a,b,c)`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.thirdMarginal_mul_condFstSndGivenThird

declarations.doc: Real-valued joint factorization for the conditional joint law: `P_C(c) * P_{A,B|C=c}(a,b) = P_{A,B,C}(a,b,c)`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.thirdMarginal_toReal_mul_condFstSndGivenThird_toReal

declarations.doc: The second marginal of the `(A,C)` law is the law of `C`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal_fstThirdMarginal

declarations.doc: The second marginal of the `(B,C)` law is the law of `C`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal_sndThirdMarginal

declarations.doc: The first marginal of `P_{A,B|C=c}` is the conditional law `P_{A|C=c}`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstMarginal_condFstSndGivenThird

declarations.doc: The second marginal of `P_{A,B|C=c}` is the conditional law `P_{B|C=c}`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal_condFstSndGivenThird

declarations.doc: The conditional law of `(A,B)` given `C=c`, obtained by conditioning the reassociated law `((A,B),C)`, is the same as `condFstSndGivenThird`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condFstGivenSnd_pairThirdLaw_eq_condFstSndGivenThird

declarations.doc: Conditional mutual information of the fiber over `C=c`. The value is zero when `P_C(c)=0`; otherwise it is the mutual information of the conditional joint law `P_{A,B|C=c}`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfoFstSndGivenThird

declarations.doc: Zero-marginal conditioning atoms contribute zero fiber mutual information.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfoFstSndGivenThird_of_thirdMarginal_eq_zero

declarations.doc: On nonzero third-coordinate atoms, the fiber CMI is the mutual information of `P_{A,B|C=c}`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfoFstSndGivenThird_of_thirdMarginal_ne_zero

declarations.doc: Conditional mutual information can be rewritten as `H(A|C) + H(B|C) - H(A,B|C)`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfo_eq_condEntropy_marginals

declarations.doc: On a nonzero third-coordinate atom, fiber CMI is the entropy identity for the three conditional fibers: `I(A;B | C=c) = H(A|C=c) + H(B|C=c) - H(A,B|C=c)`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfoFstSndGivenThird_eq_entropy_fibers_of_ne_zero

declarations.doc: Weighted pointwise bridge between fiber CMI and the three conditional entropy fibers. The zero-marginal case is killed by the factor `P_C(c)`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.thirdMarginal_toReal_mul_condMutualInfoFstSndGivenThird

declarations.doc: Expected conditional mutual information formula: `I(A;B | C) = sum_c P_C(c) I(A;B | C=c)`. The fiber term is zero on zero-marginal `c` and otherwise the mutual information of `P_{A,B|C=c}`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfo_eq_sum_thirdMarginal_mul_condMutualInfoFstSndGivenThird

declarations.doc: Conditional relative entropy between two channels under a common input law. This is the KL divergence between the two induced joint laws. Consequently, channel values outside the support of `r` do not affect the result: their entire joint-law fiber has zero mass. No per-fiber KL convention is imposed at those null base atoms.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.conditionalKlDiv

declarations.doc: Conditional relative entropy from a channel to itself is zero.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.conditionalKlDiv_self

declarations.doc: Conditional relative entropy is the base-law-weighted sum of the fiberwise KL divergences. This identity is unconditional in `ENNReal`. An infinite KL value on a null base fiber contributes `0 * ⊤ = 0`, while an infinite KL value on an active fiber makes both sides `⊤`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.conditionalKlDiv_eq_sum

declarations.doc: Real-valued weighted-fiber formula for conditional relative entropy under support inclusion on the active base atoms: `D(W || V | r) = ∑ x, r(x) D(W_x || V_x)`. No support condition is imposed when `r x = 0`. In particular, an infinite fiber KL divergence on a null base atom contributes zero to the canonical `ENNReal` weighted sum before conversion to `Real`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.toReal_conditionalKlDiv_eq_sum

declarations.doc: KL chain rule for two finite channel-joint laws: `D(P_X P_{Y|X} || Q_X Q_{Y|X}) = D(P_X || Q_X) + D(P_{Y|X} || Q_{Y|X} | P_X)`. The conditional term is weighted by the numerator base law `p`. The identity is unconditional in `ENNReal`, including when either summand is `⊤`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.klDiv_channelJoint_eq_add_conditionalKlDiv

declarations.doc: Real-valued finite joint KL chain rule under support inclusion for the base laws and for every active numerator fiber: `D(P_X P_{Y|X} || Q_X Q_{Y|X}) = D(P_X || Q_X) + D(P_{Y|X} || Q_{Y|X} | P_X)`. The fiber condition is required only on `p.support`; an infinite fiber KL divergence at a null numerator atom does not affect the identity.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.toReal_klDiv_channelJoint_eq_add_conditionalKlDiv

declarations.doc: KL divergence is jointly convex under a common finite PMF-valued selector. The result is canonical in `ENNReal`. An inactive selector component may have infinite KL because its weighted contribution is `0 * top = 0`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.klDiv_bind_le_sum

declarations.doc: Real-valued KL joint convexity under support inclusion for every active selector component. No support condition is required when the selector mass is zero, even if that inactive component has infinite KL.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.toReal_klDiv_bind_le_sum

declarations.doc: Binary joint convexity of KL divergence. The weight is `t` on the first component and `1 - t` on the second.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.klDiv_binaryMixture_le

declarations.doc: Real-valued binary KL joint convexity with support assumptions only for components whose weights can be nonzero. At `t = 0`, only the second support implication is used; at `t = 1`, only the first is used.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.toReal_klDiv_binaryMixture_le

declarations.doc: Equality in binary KL joint convexity for an interior weight. The component support assumptions exclude infinite component divergences. Under those guards, equality holds exactly when the two component likelihood ratios agree pointwise, expressed without division by the cross-product law. When both reference masses at an atom are positive, the cross-product law is the usual equality of likelihood ratios. If one reference mass vanishes, support inclusion forces its corresponding numerator mass to vanish, so the division-free statement handles the absent component without assigning a meaning to `0 / 0`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.klDiv_binaryMixture_eq_iff

declarations.doc: Real-valued equality in binary KL joint convexity for an interior weight. The same component support assumptions make every KL divergence finite, so the exact cross-product characterization is preserved by `ENNReal.toReal`. The division-free condition has the same null-mass interpretation as the canonical `ENNReal` theorem: a component absent at an atom contributes matching zero numerator and reference masses rather than an artificial likelihood ratio.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.toReal_klDiv_binaryMixture_eq_iff

declarations.doc: Mutual information across a finite PMF-valued channel is output entropy minus the input-weighted entropy of the channel laws.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_channelJoint_eq_entropy_bind_sub_sum

declarations.doc: For a fixed finite channel, mutual information is concave in the input law under a common finite PMF-valued selector.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sum_mul_mutualInfo_channelJoint_le

declarations.doc: For a fixed finite channel, mutual information is concave along a binary mixture of input laws.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_binaryMixture_input_concave

declarations.doc: For a fixed finite input law, mutual information is convex under a common finite PMF-valued selector of channels.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_channelMixture_le_sum

declarations.doc: For a fixed finite input law, mutual information is convex along a binary mixture of channels.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_binaryChannelMixture_le

declarations.doc: The mathlib kernel associated to a countable PMF-valued channel. This is a semantic view of the existing raw channel function, not a second public channel representation.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.pmfChannelKernel

declarations.doc: A PMF-valued channel induces a Markov kernel through `pmfChannelKernel`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.pmfChannelKernel.instIsMarkovKernel

declarations.doc: Evaluating the kernel associated to a PMF channel recovers its PMF measure.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.pmfChannelKernel_apply

declarations.doc: The measure of an induced PMF joint law is the composition-product of the input measure and the associated Markov kernel.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.channelJoint_toMeasure

declarations.doc: The total posterior channel associated to an input law and a finite stochastic channel. On an output atom of positive probability this is the usual posterior input law. On a null output fiber it uses the fallback already documented by `condFstGivenSndChannel`; reconstruction makes that arbitrary branch semantically irrelevant.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.channelPosterior

declarations.doc: Sampling the posterior from the channel output law reconstructs the induced joint law in output-input order.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.channelPosterior_reconstructs_joint

declarations.doc: A finite-input channel is sufficient for a model family exactly when one parameter-independent posterior channel agrees with every model posterior on each supported output fiber. Writing `Q_t = (model t).bind W`, the witness `R` satisfies `channelPosterior (model t) W b = R b` whenever `Q_t b != 0`. Consequently, two models supporting the same output have the same posterior there. A model for which `b` is null imposes no condition, although another supporting model may determine `R b`; if `b` is null for the entire family, that row is wholly unconstrained. The support guard prevents the arbitrary fallback used by the total posterior on a null fiber from acquiring conditional-probability meaning.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isSufficientChannel_iff_exists_common_posterior

declarations.doc: Exact KL decomposition for two input laws passed through the same finite stochastic channel. The first term is the divergence between the output laws. The remainder is the divergence between the two posterior kernels over the first output law, stated with mathlib composition-product measures. No support-inclusion assumption is needed because the identity is `ENNReal`-valued.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.klDiv_channel_eq_add_posterior

declarations.doc: Finite relative entropy contracts when two input laws pass through the same stochastic channel. This is the primary channel data-processing inequality. It is unconditional because KL divergence is valued in `ENNReal`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.klDiv_channel_le

declarations.doc: Equality in finite KL data processing holds exactly when the two posterior kernels agree almost everywhere under the first output law. Input support inclusion excludes the uninformative infinite-divergence case. This is the measure-level equality bridge; finite pointwise posterior forms can be derived by replacing almost-everywhere equality with equality on supported output atoms.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.klDiv_channel_eq_iff_posterior_ae_eq

declarations.doc: Equality in finite KL data processing holds exactly when the two posterior PMFs agree on every output atom reached by the first input law. This is the primary finite-facing equality theorem. The input support condition excludes infinite KL divergence, while the output support condition in the conclusion leaves the total posterior's arbitrary null-fiber values irrelevant.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.klDiv_channel_eq_iff_posterior_eq_on_support

declarations.doc: Real-valued finite relative entropy contracts through a common stochastic channel when the first input law is supported by the second. Only the input support condition is needed; no separate support hypothesis on the output laws is required.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.toReal_klDiv_channel_le

declarations.doc: Equality in real-valued finite KL data processing holds exactly when the two posterior PMFs agree on every output atom reached by the first input law. Input support inclusion makes both KL divergences finite, so this theorem has no `ENNReal.toReal` top-branch ambiguity.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.toReal_klDiv_channel_eq_iff_posterior_eq_on_support

declarations.doc: KL data processing for a deterministic map of a finite alphabet.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.klDiv_map_le

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.toReal_klDiv_map_le

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.klDiv_channel_cascade_le

declarations.doc: Textbook-facing alias for real-valued KL contraction along a cascade.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.toReal_klDiv_channel_cascade_le

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.klDiv_channel_invariant_le

declarations.doc: Real-valued KL divergence to an invariant reference law contracts when the input law is supported by that reference.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.toReal_klDiv_channel_invariant_le

declarations.doc: A finite channel that preserves the uniform law cannot decrease Shannon entropy. The discrete measurable structure used by the KL proof remains local, so the statement has only the natural finite nonempty alphabet assumptions.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_le_entropy_bind_of_uniform_invariant

declarations.doc: A finite doubly stochastic channel cannot decrease Shannon entropy. Each `W a` is already a probability law, hence supplies the row-stochastic condition. The displayed hypothesis is the remaining column-sum condition. No transition-matrix representation is introduced.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_le_entropy_bind_of_doublyStochastic

declarations.doc: Self-information of an atom under a finite PMF, in nats. It is `-log p(a)` when the real mass of `a` is nonzero, and `0` on zero-mass atoms. The zero branch is the usual entropy convention that zero-probability outcomes contribute no expected information.

declarations.doc: A zero-mass atom has zero self-information by convention.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.selfInfo_of_toReal_eq_zero

declarations.doc: A nonzero-mass atom has self-information `-log p(a)`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.selfInfo_of_toReal_ne_zero

declarations.doc: Multiplying self-information by the atom mass recovers the `Real.negMulLog` entropy summand.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.toReal_mul_selfInfo

declarations.doc: Semantic bridge for finite entropy: the finite-sum definition of `Shannon.entropy` is the expected self-information with respect to `PMF.toMeasure`. Informally, this is the textbook identity `H(P) = E[-log P(X)]`, with the zero-mass convention handled by `selfInfo`.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_eq_integral_selfInfo

declarations.doc: Entropy is monotone under inclusion of finite family atoms.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropy_mono

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropyOf_mono

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondEntropy_nonneg

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropy_submodular

declarations.doc: Entropy of finite source-indexed family atoms is submodular.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropyOf_submodular

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfo_nonneg

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfoOf_nonneg

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfo_le_entropy_right

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfoOf_le_entropyOf_left

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfoOf_le_entropyOf_right

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondEntropy_le_entropy

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondEntropyOf_le_entropyOf

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondEntropyOf_union_le_condEntropyOf

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropy_union_le_add

declarations.doc: Source-family entropy of a union of two finite atoms is subadditive.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropyOf_union_le_add

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropy_le_sum_singletons

declarations.doc: Source-family entropy is at most the sum of the selected singleton entropies.
declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropyOf_le_sum_singletons
